issues.legal_issue: A contract styled as a forest lease constitutes a sale of goods for sales-tax purposes when, in substance, it transfers the right to cut and remove specified timber that is to be severed under the contract.
material_facts: The contract allowed the buyer to cut and remove specified species of timber and required payment calculated by the timber extracted and removed.
The buyer received no possession of the forest land as land; its rights extended only to the specified timber, and other contractors could work in the same area.
The timber remained the State's property until severance, when ownership passed to the buyer.
issues.conclusion: The transaction was a sale of bamboo and salai wood under the contract, notwithstanding its description as a lease, and the Forest Department was liable to sales tax on those sales.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 2(7) of the Sale of Goods Act and section 2(g) of the Madhya Pradesh General Sales Tax Act, trees agreed to be severed before or under a contract of sale are goods. Standing timber is movable property for this purpose if it is to be severed while it still belongs to the contracting seller. The sale, sale-price and turnover definitions in sections 2(n), 2(o) and 2(t) of the Madhya Pradesh Act apply where the contract transfers the timber for consideration. The Court distinguished Raja Bahadur Kamakshya Narain Singh, which concerned income tax and a different deed, and treated Badri Prasad as recognizing that trees to be severed are goods, while distinguishing its facts.

predicates.sales_tax_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning sales tax claimed on timber transferred under an agreement styled as a lease.
predicates.specified_timber_is_to_be_severed_under_: The agreement identifies timber that the buyer is to cut or sever pursuant to the agreement.
predicates.timber_remains_seller_property_until_sev: The seller retains ownership of the timber until the buyer severs it.
predicates.buyer_lacks_possession_of_land_as_land: The buyer is not given possession of the land itself as land.
predicates.buyer_rights_are_limited_to_cutting_and_: The buyer's rights in the area are confined to cutting and removing specified timber.

issues.definition: When a sales-tax appeal concerns specified timber to be severed under an agreement, the seller retains it until severance, and the buyer lacks possession of the land or has rights confined to removing timber, the agreement is treated as a sale of goods for sales-tax purposes.

issues.legal_issue: A statutory amendment deeming a government forest department to be a dealer may be applied where a constitutional equality challenge to that amendment is unavailable in the proceeding.
material_facts: After the High Court's decision, the legislature amended the sales-tax law to alter the definition of dealer and undo the effect of the finding that the Forest Department was not a dealer.
A Presidential Proclamation had suspended the operation of Article 14, preventing the respondent from pursuing its equality challenge in this appeal.
issues.conclusion: The amendment was to be applied in this appeal, and the Forest Department was to be treated as a dealer; the Court left open any challenge to the amendment after the suspension of Article 14 ended.
issues.legal_principle: The Madhya Pradesh General Sales Tax (Amendment and Validation) Act 13 of 1971 amended the dealer definition so that the Forest Department was deemed to be a dealer. Because the operation of Article 14 of the Constitution had been suspended by Presidential Proclamation, the Court held that the equality-based challenge was unavailable in this appeal and proceeded on the basis that the amendment applied, without deciding its post-suspension validity.

predicates.sales_tax_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning sales tax liability asserted against a public body.
predicates.statutory_change_deems_public_body_a_dea: A statutory change applicable to the proceeding deems the public body to be a dealer for sales-tax purposes.
predicates.equality_challenge_unavailable_in_procee: A constitutional equality challenge to that statutory change cannot be pursued in the proceeding.

issues.definition: In a sales-tax appeal, when an applicable statutory change deems a public body to be a dealer and an equality challenge to the change is unavailable, the body is treated as a dealer in that proceeding.

issues.legal_issue: A buyer required to reimburse sales tax under the statutory pass-through of a seller's tax liability is liable only for the amount the seller is legally liable to pay, and a disputed amount must be determined before recovery from the buyer.
material_facts: Both the Forest Department and the respondent were registered dealers.
The State relied on section 64-A of the Sale of Goods Act to recover from the respondent tax payable by the Forest Department on the timber sales.

The respondent disputed the amount claimed, including the applicable tax rate, and the amount had been pursued through revenue-recovery proceedings that had deprived it of an opportunity to challenge the calculation.

The State agreed that the respondent should be allowed to establish the legally recoverable amount; the State also sought to raise the respondent's failure to provide a requested declaration before the High Court.
issues.conclusion: The case was remanded for determination of the amount of tax the Forest Department was legally liable to pay, with the respondent able to contest the quantification and the State able to raise the declaration issue before the High Court; the respondent would pay only after the tax amount was settled.
issues.legal_principle: Section 64-A of the Sale of Goods Act permits the seller, in the circumstances it specifies, to recover from the buyer sales tax that the seller has had to pay. The buyer cannot be required to reimburse more than the seller's legally payable tax. The applicable rate and the tax calculation therefore had to be determined, and the buyer had to have an opportunity to challenge the amount. The Court remanded that limited issue.

rule.if: sales_tax_appeal and seller_seeks_to_pass_through_tax_to_buyer and buyer_disputes_amount and seller_tax_liability_has_not_been_quantified

predicates.sales_tax_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning a seller's attempt to recover sales tax from a buyer.
predicates.seller_seeks_to_pass_through_tax_to_buye: The seller seeks to make the buyer reimburse tax that the seller is liable to pay.
predicates.buyer_disputes_amount: The buyer disputes whether the amount claimed is correctly calculated or legally payable.
predicates.seller_tax_liability_has_not_been_quanti: The seller's lawful tax liability has not yet been determined.

issues.definition: When a seller seeks to pass tax on to a buyer in a sales-tax appeal, the buyer disputes the claim, and the seller's liability is not quantified, the seller's lawful liability must be determined before the buyer is required to pay.

issues.legal_issue: The Court need not reconsider the existing finding about recovery of the tax as arrears of land revenue when the tax amount must first be settled.
material_facts: The tax had been pursued through revenue-recovery proceedings as if it were land revenue.
The High Court's treatment of whether the sales tax was recoverable as arrears of land revenue had not been properly adjudicated.
The Court remanded the case to settle the amount of tax legally payable and stated that it was not upsetting the High Court's finding on the recovery method.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to reconsider the recovery-as-land-revenue issue in this appeal and did not disturb the High Court's finding on that point.
issues.legal_principle: The Court treated determination of the lawful tax amount as the issue requiring remand and considered it unnecessary to reopen the recovery method at that stage; it expressly left the High Court's finding undisturbed.

predicates.sales_tax_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning the assessment or recovery of sales tax.
predicates.tax_amount_requires_determination: The amount of tax legally payable remains to be determined.
predicates.existing_finding_addresses_recovery_as_l: The lower court has made a finding concerning recovery of the tax as arrears of land revenue.

issues.definition: When a sales-tax appeal requires the tax amount to be determined and the lower court has addressed recovery as land revenue, the existing recovery finding is left undisturbed.
